sentences.en: Good morning everyone.
sentences.zh: 大家早上好。

sentences.en: So today we're going to look at an important creative activity and that's hand knitting.
sentences.zh: 那么，今天我们将探讨一项重要的创意活动——手工编织（针织）。

sentences.en: Ancient knitted garments have been found in many different countries, showing that knitting is a global activity with a long history.
sentences.zh: 在许多不同国家都发现了古代的针织服装，这表明针织是一项具有悠久历史的全球性活动。

sentences.en: When someone says the word ‘knitting' we might well picture an elderly person- a grandmother perhaps- sitting bv the fire knitting garments for themselves or other members of the family.
sentences.zh: 当有人提到‘针织’这个词时，我们很可能会联想到一位老年人——也许是一位祖母——坐在炉火旁，为自己或家人编织衣物。

sentences.en: It's a homely image, but one that may lead you to feel that knitting is an activity of the past- and, indeed, during the previous decade, it was one of the skills that was predicted to vanish from everyday life.
sentences.zh: 这是一个温馨的画面，但这种印象可能让你觉得针织是属于过去的活动；事实上，在过去十年间，它曾被预测会从日常生活中消失。

sentences.en: For although humans have sewn and knitted their own clothing for a very long time, many of these craft-based skills went into decline when industrial machines took over- mainly because they were no longer passed down from one generation to another.
sentences.zh: 尽管人类缝制和编织自己衣物的历史非常悠久，但当工业机器接管后，许多这类手工艺技能便逐渐衰落——主要原因在于它们不再代代相传。

sentences.en: However, that's all changing and interest in knitting classes in many countries is actually rising, as more and more people are seeking formal instruction in the skill.
sentences.zh: 然而，这种情况正在改变，许多国家的针织课程兴趣实际上正在上升，越来越多的人开始寻求这项技能的正规指导。

sentences.en: With that trend, we're also seeing an increase in the sales figures for knitting equipment.
sentences.zh: 随着这一趋势，针织设备的销售数据也在增加。

sentences.en: So why do people want to be taught to knit at a time when a machine can readily do the job for them?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么在机器能轻易完成这项工作的时候，人们仍想学习针织呢？

sentences.en: The answer is that knitting, as a handicraft, has numerous benefits for those doing it.
sentences.zh: 答案是：作为一门手工艺，针织对实践者有着诸多益处。

sentences.en: Let's consider what some of these might be.
sentences.zh: 让我们来思考其中一些可能的益处。

sentences.en: While many people knitted garments in the past because they couldn't afford to buy clothes, it's still true today that knitting can be helpful if vou're experiencing economic hardship.
sentences.zh: 过去许多人织衣物是因为买不起衣服，而如今，针织在你面临经济困难时依然可能有所帮助。

sentences.en: If you have several children who all need warm Audioscripts winter clothes, knitting may save you a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 如果你有几个孩子，都需要保暖的冬季服装，那么自己编织或许能为你节省一大笔钱。

sentences.en: And the results of knitting your own clothes can be very rewarding, even though the skills you need to get going are really quite basic and the financial outlay is minimal.
sentences.zh: 而且，亲手制作自己的衣物成果非常有成就感，即使入门所需技能其实相当基础，且初期投入的资金也极少。

sentences.en: But the more significant benefits in today's world are to do with well-being.
sentences.zh: 但在当今世界，更显著的益处则与身心健康相关。

sentences.en: In a world where it's estimated that we spend up to nine hours a day online, doing something with our hands that is craft-based makes us feel good.
sentences.zh: 在一个据估计我们每天上网时间长达九小时的世界里，从事一种以手工为基础的手工艺活动能让我们感觉良好。

sentences.en: It releases us from the stress of a technological, fast- paced life.
sentences.zh: 它使我们摆脱技术化、快节奏生活所带来的压力。

sentences.en: Now, let's look back a bit to early knitting activities.
sentences.zh: 现在，让我们回溯一下早期的针织活动。

sentences.en: In fact, no one really knows when knitting first began, but archaeological remains have disclosed plenty of information for us to think about.
sentences.zh: 事实上，没有人真正知道针织究竟始于何时，但考古遗存已为我们提供了大量可供思考的信息。

sentences.en: One of the interesting things about knitting is that the earliest pieces of clothing that have been found suggest that most of the items produced were round rather than flat.
sentences.zh: 针织一个有趣之处在于：迄今发现的最早期服装表明，当时所生产的物品大多呈圆形而非扁平状。

sentences.en: Discoveries from the 3rd and 4th centuries in Egypt show that things like socks and gloves, that were needed to keep hands and feet warm, were knitted in one piece using four or five needles.
sentences.zh: 公元3至4世纪埃及的考古发现显示，诸如袜子和手套等用于保暖手足的物品，是用四根或五根针一次性编织而成的。

sentences.en: That's very different from most knitting patterns today, which only require two.
sentences.zh: 这与当今大多数只需两根针的针织图样大不相同。

sentences.en: What's more, the very first needles people used were hand carved out of wood and other natural materials, like bone, whereas today's needles are largely made of steel or plastic and make that characteristic clicking sound when someone's using them.Ancient people knitted using yams made from linen, hemp, cotton and wool, and these were often very rough on the skin.
sentences.zh: 此外，人们最初使用的针是手工雕刻的木制或其他天然材料（如骨头）制成的；而如今的针则主要由钢或塑料制成，使用时会发出特有的咔嗒声。古代人使用的纱线由亚麻、大麻、棉和羊毛制成，这些材质往往对皮肤非常粗糙。

sentences.en: The spinning wheel, which allowed people to make finer yarns and produce much greater quantities of them, led to the dominance of wool in the knitting industry- often favoured for its warmth.
sentences.zh: 纺车的出现使人们能够纺出更精细的纱线，并大幅提高产量，从而促使羊毛在针织行业中占据主导地位——人们通常因其保暖性而偏爱羊毛。

sentences.en: Another interesting fact about knitting is that because it was practised in so many parts of the world for so many purposes, regional differences in style developed.
sentences.zh: 关于针织的另一个有趣事实是：由于它在世界各地被广泛应用于多种目的，各地逐渐发展出风格各异的区域特色。

sentences.en: This visual identity has allowed researchers to match bits of knitted clothing that have been unearthed over time to the region from which the wearer came or the job that he or she did.
sentences.zh: 这种视觉上的独特性使研究人员得以将不同时期出土的针织衣物碎片，与其穿着者来源地或职业相匹配。

sentences.en: As I've mentioned, knitting offered people from poor communities a way of making extra money while doing other tasks.
sentences.zh: 正如我之前所提到的，针织曾为贫困社区的人们提供了一种在从事其他任务的同时赚取额外收入的方式。

sentences.en: For many centuries, it seems, men, women and children took every opportunity to knit, for example, while watching over sheep, walking to market or riding in boats.
sentences.zh: 看来在数个世纪以来，无论男女老少都抓住一切机会进行编织，例如放羊时、步行去市场途中，或乘船航行时。

sentences.en: So, let's move on to take a ...
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们继续……
